newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures called higher on SW heat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures called higher on SW heat.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher after Friday's rise on outlook of strong cooling demand in the Southwest and talk of capacity reduction on the Pacific Intertie transmission system.

In over-the-counter business, July Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $28.25-28.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Friday's settlement at $27.68, while July California-Oregon Border (COB) at $18.00-18.50 against Friday's close at $17.80.
Meterologists called for seasonal weather across the West this week and summer-like weather the following week.
Coastal cities from Seattle to San Diego would see temperatures in the 70s F, while inland centers like Phoenix and Tuscon would be covered by triple-digit heat by mid-week.

A Western Systems Coordinating Council committee this week is expected to propose a summertime rating for the Pacific Intertie at 6,900 megawatt (MW), 300 MW below from current level to insure electricity reliability.
In the meantime, Bonneville Power Administration suggested summer transmission capacity on the intertie be reduced to 6,300 megawatts (MW) from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
PV contracts may receive a boost from strength in natural gas futures, market sources said. The July Henry Hub gas contract opened up 1.6 cent at $2.165 per million British thermal units.
Higher power demand and reduced supply in the Southwest are expected to be offset by a slate of cheap coal-fired generation returning to service.
About 3,000 MW of coal-fired capacity were planned to restart over the week after unplanned repair shutdowns and planned maintenance outages.

Those units include a 450 MW San Juan unit in New Mexico, a 750 MW Four Corners unit also in New Mexico, a 300 MW Reid Gardner unit in Nevada, a 190 MW Hayden unit in Colorado, a 670 MW Centralia unit in Washington and a 875 MW Intermountain unit in Utah.
Moreover, the 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was expected to resume power production next week, ahead of an original schedule.
